section: Communal violence - major episodes, consequences and remedies
subsections: Consequences - ghettoisation, displacement, loss of trust, polarisation
Remedies - Communal Violence Bill (draft), National Integration Council, peace committees

accepted.s: Which commission was appointed to inquire into the demolition of the disputed structure at Ayodhya on 6 December 1992?
accepted.x: The Liberhan Commission investigated the demolition of the disputed structure at Ayodhya on 6 December 1992.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the commission from the matter it was constituted to probe.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Liberhan Commission:
1. It was a one-man commission.
2. It was set up on 16 December 1992.
3. Justice M.S. Liberhan died at the age of 87 in August 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the commission was a one-man commission established on 16 December 1992, and Justice M.S. Liberhan died aged 87 in August 2026.
accepted.tq: Check each date, numerical detail and institutional description separately.

accepted.s: The Srikrishna Commission primarily investigated which of the following?
accepted.x: The Srikrishna Commission investigated the Bombay, now Mumbai, riots of 1992–93 and found failure of state administration.
accepted.tq: Use the commission–riot pair rather than confusing it with other inquiry commissions.

accepted.s: The Nanavati Commission, constituted in 2000, is associated with the inquiry into the
accepted.x: The Nanavati Commission of 2000 investigated the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. Its report was submitted in February 2005, after which Jagdish Tytler resigned.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly named commissions by their year and subject.

accepted.s: With reference to the Nanavati Commission, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It investigated the conspiracy behind Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination.
Its report was submitted in February 2005 and Jagdish Tytler resigned after it.
It was set up by the Gujarat Government to investigate the Godhra train burning.
It examined the social and educational status of Muslims.
accepted.x: The Nanavati Commission submitted its report in February 2005, following which Jagdish Tytler resigned. The other statements refer to different inquiries or committees.
accepted.tq: Separate nearby commission facts by matching the correct consequence to the correct body.

accepted.s: The Nanavati-Mehta Commission, constituted in 2002, was set up by the Gujarat Government to inquire into the
o: Gujarat riots of 2002, including the Godhra train burning
accepted.x: The Nanavati-Mehta Commission was set up by the Gujarat Government to inquire into the Gujarat riots of 2002 and the Godhra train burning.
accepted.tq: The trap is the similar name of the Nanavati Commission, which concerned the 1984 riots.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ranganath Misra Commission (1985) — 1984 anti-Sikh riots and Punjab Accord
Ranganath Misra Commission — demolition of the disputed structure at Ayodhya
Wadhwa Commission — conspiracy behind Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination
Jain Commission — murder of Graham Staines
accepted.x: The Ranganath Misra Commission of 1985 examined the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in the context of the Punjab Accord. The Wadhwa Commission concerned Graham Staines’ murder, while the Jain Commission examined the conspiracy behind Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure commission–subject pair and eliminate swapped investigators.

accepted.s: The Ranganath Misra Commission associated with the National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities submitted its report in
accepted.x: The Ranganath Misra Commission associated with the National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities submitted its report in 2007 and examined backward sections among religious and linguistic minorities.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two Ranganath Misra references by subject and report year.

accepted.s: The Wadhwa Commission and the Jain Commission were respectively associated with which of the following?
o: Graham Staines’ murder and the conspiracy behind Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination
Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination and the 1984 anti-Sikh riots
The Gujarat riots and the Babri demolition
The Bombay riots and the Gujarat riots
accepted.x: The Wadhwa Commission examined the murder of missionary Graham Staines in Odisha in 1999, whereas the Jain Commission examined the conspiracy behind Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination.
accepted.tq: Match each commission to its distinctive subject, avoiding reversal of the pairs.

accepted.s: The Sachar Committee, constituted in March 2005 under the chairmanship of Rajinder Sachar, was a
o: Committee on the rehabilitation of riot victims
Commission on the linguistic reorganisation of States
Prime Minister’s High Level Committee on the social, economic and educational status of Muslims
accepted.x: The Sachar Committee was the Prime Minister’s High Level Committee on the social, economic and educational status of Muslims, chaired by Rajinder Sachar and constituted in March 2005.
accepted.tq: Combine the chairperson, date and mandate to identify the committee precisely.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Moradabad riots occurred in 1980 in Uttar Pradesh, not Bihar. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong state while keeping the year–event pair in view.

accepted.s: The Direct Action Day and Noakhali violence of 1946 were associated with
accepted.x: The Direct Action Day and Noakhali violence occurred in 1946 in Bengal, including Calcutta and Noakhali.
accepted.tq: Identify the geographical cluster rather than treating Calcutta and Noakhali as separate states.

accepted.s: Partition riots of 1947 were particularly associated with which regions?
accepted.x: The Partition riots of 1947 were associated especially with Punjab and Bengal.
accepted.tq: Use the two-region pairing as the distinguishing feature.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following communal disturbances in chronological order:
A. Ahmedabad riots
B. Jabalpur riots
C. Moradabad riots
D. Bhagalpur riots
accepted.x: The correct order is Jabalpur (1961), Ahmedabad (1969), Moradabad (1980) and Bhagalpur (1989).
accepted.tq: Place the earliest and latest events first, then arrange the middle years.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Anti-Sikh riots — 1984 — Delhi, also Kanpur and Bokaro
accepted.x: The anti-Sikh riots occurred in 1984, chiefly in Delhi, with violence also reported in Kanpur and Bokaro. Meerut was in Uttar Pradesh, Bhagalpur in Bihar and Kokrajhar in Assam.
accepted.tq: Check both the year and the state, since the distractors swap locations.

accepted.s: The Babri demolition aftermath of 1992–93 was associated with violence in
o: Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh, Mumbai and other places
accepted.x: The aftermath of the Babri demolition involved Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh, Mumbai and other places during 1992–93.
accepted.tq: Avoid the single-location trap by recalling the wider geographical spread.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Delhi riots of 2020 occurred in North-East Delhi, not North-West Delhi. The other pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Test the precise directional location rather than accepting the familiar city name alone.

accepted.s: The communal violence recorded in Manipur in the given chronology belongs to the year
accepted.x: The Manipur communal violence listed in the chronology belongs to 2023.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among the closely placed recent years in the chronology.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Partition is correct?
o: Approximately 40 million people crossed the borders, and historians generally estimate 50 lakh deaths.
Population movement was limited to Punjab and did not affect Bengal.
Approximately 14–18 million people crossed the borders, and estimates of deaths range from 2 lakh to 20 lakh.
Fewer than one million people crossed the borders, and deaths were uniformly estimated at 2 lakh.
accepted.x: An estimated 14–18 million people crossed the borders during Partition. Estimates of deaths range from 2 lakh to 20 lakh, with many historians placing the figure near 10 lakh.
accepted.tq: Retain both the migration range and the death-estimate range without narrowing them incorrectly.

accepted.s:
With reference to the Gujarat riots of 2002, consider the following statements:
1. Fifty-nine people, mostly kar sevaks, were burnt on the Sabarmati Express near Godhra.
2. The incident occurred on 27 February 2002.
3. An investigation was conducted by a Special Investigation Team appointed by the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Godhra train burning involved 59 people, mostly kar sevaks, occurred on 27 February 2002, and was investigated by an SC-appointed SIT.
accepted.tq: Verify the event, date and investigating authority independently.

accepted.s: How many people were reported killed in the riots that followed the Godhra train burning in 2002?
accepted.x: The number recorded for those killed in the riots that followed the Godhra train burning was 1,169.
accepted.tq: Use the exact quantitative figure and distinguish it from the 59 deaths on the train.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a characteristic of communal riots?
o: They occur exclusively in rural areas and are unrelated to religious festivals.
They are more common in North India.
They may be politically and economically motivated.
They often recur in riot-prone towns and may be triggered during religious festivals.
accepted.x: Communal riots are not confined exclusively to rural areas and may be triggered during religious festivals. The other three are recognised features.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme statement containing ‘exclusively’ and ‘unrelated’.

accepted.s: Ghettoisation following communal riots refers to the
o: temporary migration of workers to industrial areas
legal segregation of citizens by the State
movement of communities into religiously segregated neighbourhoods
division of a district into administrative wards
accepted.x: Ghettoisation is the movement of communities into religiously segregated neighbourhoods after communal violence.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a social consequence from formal legal or administrative segregation.
accepted.sec: Consequences - ghettoisation, displacement, loss of trust, polarisation

accepted.s: The Partition of India is described as the
o: first organised rural resettlement in South Asia
largest voluntary migration in the twentieth century
first instance of international migration in Asia
accepted.x: Partition is described as the largest forced migration in history.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise descriptor and reject the voluntary-migration reversal.
accepted.sec: Consequences - ghettoisation, displacement, loss of trust, polarisation

accepted.s: Which of the following best represents the consequence of communal violence for trust in institutions?
o: It eliminates the need for legal accountability.
It affects only electoral institutions and not the rule of law.
It may produce insecurity, instability and loss of faith in the police and courts.
It invariably increases faith in the police and courts.
accepted.x: Communal violence can undermine the rule of law by producing insecurity, instability and loss of faith in the police and courts, especially when guilty persons are not brought to book.
accepted.tq: Apply the consequence to institutional trust rather than recalling only an event name.
accepted.sec: Consequences - ghettoisation, displacement, loss of trust, polarisation

accepted.s: The analysis of the impact of Partition and communal riots on women in Critical Events was undertaken by
accepted.x: Veena Das analysed the impact of Partition and communal riots on women in her work Critical Events.
accepted.tq: Match the scholar with the specific analytical theme and work.
accepted.sec: Consequences - ghettoisation, displacement, loss of trust, polarisation

accepted.s: Which of the following is a consequence of communal violence for Indian society and India’s external image?
o: Strengthening of social capital and unconditional social cohesion
Polarisation, weaker social capital, a threat to unity in diversity, and harm to India’s global image and diaspora
Removal of social divisions through permanent segregation
Improvement in the reputation of India among all diaspora communities
accepted.x: Communal violence can cause polarisation, weaken social capital, threaten unity in diversity, and harm India’s global image and the diaspora.
accepted.tq: Select the comprehensive consequence statement while rejecting reversed effects.
accepted.sec: Consequences - ghettoisation, displacement, loss of trust, polarisation

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Prevention of Communal and Targeted Violence Bill, 2011:
1. It was drafted by the National Advisory Council.
2. It was enacted into law after being passed by Parliament.
3. It was never passed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Bill was drafted by the National Advisory Council but was never passed. Therefore, statements 1 and 3 are correct and statement 2 is false.
accepted.tq: Catch the enacted-versus-draft distinction, a common status trap.
accepted.sec: Remedies - Communal Violence Bill (draft), National Integration Council, peace committees

accepted.s: The Prevention of Communal and Targeted Violence Bill, 2011 was criticised by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the ground that it sought to
o: transfer policing to the Union Government
hold the majority community responsible for riots
accepted.x: Narendra Modi described the draft Bill as one that sought to hold the majority community responsible for riots. Congress had promised a similar law in Assam.
accepted.tq: Link the political criticism to the precise feature attributed to the draft law.
accepted.sec: Remedies - Communal Violence Bill (draft), National Integration Council, peace committees

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the National Integration Council is correct?
o: It is chaired by the President and includes only Members of Parliament.
It is chaired by the Prime Minister and includes Union Ministers, Chief Ministers and eminent persons.
It is chaired by the Home Secretary and includes only police officers.
It is chaired by the Chief Justice of India and includes judges of High Courts.
accepted.x: The National Integration Council is chaired by the Prime Minister and includes Union Ministers, Chief Ministers and eminent persons. It has also been criticised as inactive.
accepted.tq: Ask who chairs the body and who forms its broad composition.
accepted.sec: Remedies - Communal Violence Bill (draft), National Integration Council, peace committees

accepted.s: The National Foundation for Communal Harmony primarily
o: supports child victims of violence and promotes inter-faith dialogue
conducts criminal trials in riot cases
appoints inquiry commissions for all communal disturbances
accepted.x: The National Foundation for Communal Harmony supports child victims of violence and promotes inter-faith dialogue.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a support-and-dialogue institution from investigative and judicial bodies.
accepted.sec: Remedies - Communal Violence Bill (draft), National Integration Council, peace committees

accepted.s:
Which of the following measures are associated with the prevention and management of communal violence?
1. Establishment of peace committees in riot-affected areas.
2. Advising the media to calm rather than inflame tensions.
3. Curtailing extremist outfits.
4. Guidelines covering prevention, containment and response.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four are recognised measures: peace committees, responsible media conduct, curbing extremist outfits and the MHA Guidelines for Communal Harmony covering prevention, containment and response.
accepted.tq: Use the comprehensive option after checking each remedy against the three stages of response.
accepted.sec: Remedies - Communal Violence Bill (draft), National Integration Council, peace committees

accepted.s: Home Guards were first raised in December 1946 primarily to
o: help the police control civil disturbance and communal riots
replace the regular police in all districts
accepted.x: Home Guards were first raised in December 1946 to assist the police in controlling civil disturbance and communal riots.
accepted.tq: Match the organisation’s origin date with its original operational purpose.
accepted.sec: Remedies - Communal Violence Bill (draft), National Integration Council, peace committees
